subject: sociology
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC A-Level Sociology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Socialisation & Culture
units.blurb: Culture, identity and an applied option topic

topics.name: Social Construction of Culture
topics.blurb: How culture is created and varies between societies

topics.name: Socialisation & Its Agencies
topics.blurb: Family, education, media and peers shaping behaviour

topics.name: Acquisition of Identity
topics.blurb: How class, gender and ethnicity form identity

topics.name: Families or Youth Cultures
topics.blurb: Optional in-depth study of family or youth subcultures

topics.name: Differentiation & Stratification
topics.blurb: Class, gender, ethnicity and age inequalities

topics.name: Theories of Stratification
topics.blurb: Functionalist, Marxist, Weberian and feminist views

topics.name: Crime, Health, Politics or World Sociology

connections.why: Culture is transmitted through the agencies of socialisation
Socialisation by family, school and media builds personal identity
Families and youth cultures are themselves key agencies of socialisation
Identity formation is explored in depth through families or youth cultures
Validity and reliability guide the choice of primary method
Method choice reflects positivist or interpretivist theory
Use of official statistics reflects a positivist methodology
Patterns of inequality are explained by competing stratification theories
The theories frame the chosen theme-of-power option
Class, gender and ethnic identity map onto structures of inequality
Sociological theory underpins both research design and stratification debates
Studying crime or health applies the methods learned in Component 2
Institutions like education reproduce social stratification
